subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: What startup SecretRef failure policy should OpenClaw use when a side-effecting exec provider fails under a process supervisor?
rationale: The current fail-fast policy is documented and security-sensitive, but supervised restarts can amplify credential-provider calls; changing it requires maintainer intent about fail-closed behavior, retry timing, operator visibility, and whether any config surface is acceptable.

options.title: Add bounded generic startup protection
options.body: Implement a core-owned, provider-agnostic startup retry/backoff or degraded-startup policy with clear logs and tests, without hardcoding 1Password behavior.

options.title: Keep fail-fast and document supervisor mitigation
options.body: Preserve the current startup contract and add stronger docs/doctor guidance for LaunchAgent/systemd restart limits and external resolver caching.

options.title: Design configurable retry policy
options.body: Add a reviewed config/API proposal for retryPolicy-style knobs and migration/docs coverage before implementation.

recommendation.title: Add bounded generic startup protection
recommendation.body: Implement a core-owned, provider-agnostic startup retry/backoff or degraded-startup policy with clear logs and tests, without hardcoding 1Password behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The core SecretRef resolver/runtime history most directly routes through this owner, and the decision affects that contract.
